name: per-layer-input-streams-and-cross-layer-kv
written_before: any code. Frozen against main 6b62f6d2, the base this branch was cut from. Immutable from here: execution-time falsifications, deviations and evidence go in gemma4-e4b-1-execution-notes.json and gemma4-e4b-1-evidence.json (both append-only, created by the first rung that has something to record). The human-readable contract is docs/gemma4-e4b-1.md; the baseline is docs/gemma4-e4b-1-reconnaissance.md. Where this file and the prose disagree on a number, this file is the authority.
scope: text_generation for google/gemma-4-E4B-it, then google/gemma-4-E2B-it. No implicit multimodal completeness: image_conditioned and audio_conditioned remain inadmissible and gain an explicit blocker (forecast F-MM below).

decisions.D1_schema: GRAPH_SCHEMA 7 only for containers that use kv_source or layer_input_stream. Existing v6 containers are untouched. New readers accept 6 and 7. The encoder writes 7 iff the graph uses at least one v7 feature, and lists every used feature in required_features.
decisions.D2_ir: Option B (typed cross-layer references: KvSource::Layer{producer: ValueRef{layer, site}} and Component.layer_input_stream), shaped to extend toward a general value graph (option C) through ValueRef.site.
decisions.D3_unused_weights: The KV-shared layers' k_proj / v_proj / k_norm are PRESERVED byte-exact with provenance, in the tensor class retained_unreachable, with a reason the graph must justify. They are never bindable as operands.
decisions.D4_semantics: PLANNER_SEMANTICS_VERSION bumps by exactly one in every rung that changes admissibility or interpretation (R2, R3, R4, R5). Executor-only rungs (R6 to R8) do not bump. Numbers are relative to whatever main carries at each merge; the base is 23 at 6b62f6d2.
decisions.D6_oracle: Primary: transformers, use_cache=True, attn_implementation=eager, float32. Secondary: Google's JAX reference (google-deepmind/gemma), spot-read and spot-checked; not a gate.

oracle_facts_read_at_freeze.hf_sharing_gate: transformers shares K/V only when past_key_values is not None (modeling_gemma4.py L1198); Gemma4TextModel.forward creates a DynamicCache when use_cache resolves true (L1558, L1571-1572). With use_cache=False the shared layers project their own K/V from the shipped weights: a different function.
oracle_facts_read_at_freeze.google_sharing_is_unconditional: _modules.py Attention returns {'k','v'} for every call ('Always cache the layer-sharing KV', L377-397) and _transformer.py passes new_cache[producer] to the consumer (L360-385) whether or not a decode cache exists. Google's function = HF use_cache=True.
oracle_facts_read_at_freeze.google_computes_and_discards_shared_kv: _modules.py L275-287: shared layers compute K/V through kv_einsum and overwrite with kv_shared_cache['k'/'v']; the TODO reads 'move the key_proj and value_proj to kv_shared_cache=None case after checkpoints remove the kv_einsum from the shared layers'. The shipped shared-layer K/V weights are vestigial by the authors' statement.
oracle_facts_read_at_freeze.producer_rules_differ: HF: the last layer before the shared region with the same layer_type (modeling_gemma4.py L1147-1159). Google: global -> num_unshared-1, local -> num_unshared-2, positional (_config.py L55-84). They agree on E4B (22 sliding, 23 full) and E2B (13, 14) only because the last two unshared layers are (sliding, full). The graph therefore carries producers explicitly and the planner checks them against the HF rule (the primary oracle's), with the Google rule recorded as a second derivation (disagreement = refusal, see P-KV2).
oracle_facts_read_at_freeze.ple_prenorm_scale_differs: HF multiplies the per-layer projection by hidden_size^-0.5 BEFORE the per-slice RMSNorm (L1667-1673); Google applies the norm directly (_modules.py L192-193); the converter does not rescale the weight (convert_gemma4_weights.py L970-976). RMSNorm is scale-invariant except through eps, so HF's effective eps is hidden_size*1e-6 (2.56e-3 on E4B, 1.536e-3 on E2B) against Google's 1e-6. The graph carries the scale explicitly as a declared pre-norm scale; HF is the primary oracle; the magnitude of the divergence is measured report-only at R6 (X-GOOGLE-1).
oracle_facts_read_at_freeze.ple_oov_token: Google maps token ids outside the text vocabulary to 0 (_modules.py L188-191); HF maps multimodal positions to pad_token_id (0 in both configs). Same value for these checkpoints; out of scope (text only).
oracle_facts_read_at_freeze.double_wide: Google: override_kv_shared_ffw_hidden = embed_dim*FFW_RATIO*2 on KV-shared layers when enabled (E2B True, E4B False; _gemma4.py L115-148, L185); HF: intermediate_size*2 on KV-shared layers (L1016-1024). Same layers, same widths.

metric_definitions.logits: final logits after final_logit_softcapping (30.0), captured as f32 on both sides
metric_definitions.logprob: log_softmax over the FULL vocabulary (262144), computed in float64 from the f32 logits, independently on each side
metric_definitions.max_abs_dlogprob: max over every vocabulary entry v of |logprob_larql[v] - logprob_hf[v]| at one position; the gate applies at every scored position
metric_definitions.top5_ordered: the 5 highest-logprob token ids in descending order, ties in logprob broken by lower token id, on each side
metric_definitions.near_tie_rule: for HF's ordered top-5 (h1..h5) the margin m_k = logprob_hf[h_k] - logprob_hf[h_{k+1}] for k = 1..4, plus m_5 = logprob_hf[h5] - logprob_hf[h6]. LARQL's ordered top-5 must equal HF's, except that a transposition of an adjacent pair (k, k+1) with m_k <= tau is recorded as tie_swap{position, k, m_k}, and a membership change at rank 5 with m_5 <= tau is recorded as tie_swap{position, 5, m_5}. Anything else (a non-adjacent reorder, a membership change at rank 5 with m_5 > tau, or any difference with margin > tau) FAILS. Every position records m_1..m_5 whether or not it swapped
metric_definitions.plane: the residual entering layer 0 (embedding output, after embed_scale) is plane 0, and the residual leaving layer i (after layer_scalar) is plane i+1, as in scripts/dump_layers_hf.py
metric_definitions.rel_l2: ||h_larql - h_hf||_2 / ||h_hf||_2 per (plane, position), computed in float64
metric_definitions.cosine: cos(h_larql, h_hf) per (plane, position), computed in float64
metric_definitions.ple_tap: the combined per-layer input (after the 2^-0.5 combine), per (position, layer slice of 256): rel_l2 against HF's project_per_layer_inputs output
metric_definitions.kv_tap_internal: the K and V rows the consumer's attention kernel reads at (consumer layer, position): must be the producer's stored rows, bit-identical, and on device backends the same buffer object
metric_definitions.kv_tap_oracle: the producer's post-norm post-RoPE K and post-norm V rows vs HF past_key_values.shared_layers[producer]: rel_l2 per (row)
metric_definitions.greedy_prefix: the number of leading generated ids identical between LARQL greedy and HF greedy (generate do_sample=False, use_cache=True)

V1_reference_vs_hf.precedent: Gemma 4 26B-A4B reference vs HF f32: rel_rms 1e-6..8e-6, cos 1.000000000 on all 30 layers (ROADMAP.md, G4.1+G4.2)

tolerances.V4_cached_decode_vs_hf: V1 tolerances, at matching absolute positions, against HF's FRESH full-sequence forward

V5_lowered_metal_vs_reference.precedent: G4.3 gate, carried verbatim: layer-diff lowered vs interpreter <= 1e-6
V5_lowered_metal_vs_reference.note: if this precedent does not hold on a 42-layer BF16 container it is a recorded finding in execution notes, and the gate is not relaxed in place

tolerances.greedy: for each chat prompt, LARQL's greedy ids equal HF's up to the first position at which HF's m_1 <= tau; a divergence before that position FAILS; after it the remainder is report-only
tolerances.oracle_self_consistency: HF cached decode vs HF fresh forward at matching positions: REPORT-ONLY. If it exceeds V1 tolerances, record an instrument note; LARQL is gated against the FRESH forward

prompt_bank_chat.template: the checkpoint's chat_template.jinja (blob pinned above), a single user turn, add_generation_prompt=True
prompt_bank_chat.token_ids_authority: LARQL tokenises once with the pinned tokenizer; the ids are written to gemma4-e4b-1-token-bank.json and committed BEFORE the first oracle comparison, and both sides consume those ids (the dump_layers_hf.py rule: only one side chooses tokens)

long_sequences.source: the passage pinned under pins.text_source_for_long_sequences, tokenised once without a chat template, with BOS, then truncated; the ids are committed in the token bank with the chat prompts
long_sequences.scored_positions: every position of every length; the harness streams metrics per position and stores summaries, the ordered top-5, the margins m_1..m_5 and per-plane rel_l2/cosine; it does not store full logits

teacher_forced_decode.why: crosses the 512 sliding window inside decode, on producer 22 and every sliding consumer

long_sequences.decode_tokens: the next tokens of the same passage, identical on both sides (teacher forcing). Never sampled
comparisons: C-FRESH: LARQL fresh prefill at L vs HF fresh forward at L, every position
C-DECODE: LARQL cached decode at each decode position vs HF fresh forward over the same full sequence, at the matching absolute position
C-SELF: LARQL cached decode vs LARQL fresh prefill at the same position (V4 internal)
C-CHUNK: each chunking vs whole prefill, LARQL internal, V4 tolerances
C-ORACLE-SELF: HF cached decode vs HF fresh, report-only

controls_that_must_fail.NC-KV: LARQL (correct) vs HF with use_cache=False (shared layers project their own K/V). Must FAIL V1 at some position at or beyond the first shared layer's influence; if it passes, the instrument cannot see sharing and every V1 pass is void
controls_that_must_fail.NC-PLE: LARQL (correct) vs HF with per_layer_inputs forced to zero (hooked on the oracle side). Must FAIL V1; if it passes, the instrument cannot see the stream
controls_that_must_fail.NC-RETAINED: an op plan forged to bind a retained_unreachable tensor must be REFUSED at open with RetainedTensorBound (P-PRES3)
controls_that_must_fail.why_on_the_oracle_side: the wrong arms for NC-KV and NC-PLE are produced by the oracle, never by binding retained tensors in LARQL, so the unreachability property is never weakened to build a control

K1_producer.rule: KvSource::Layer{producer: ValueRef{layer, site: AttentionKv}}: producer.layer < consumer, same component, producer is KvSource::Own, no chains
tests: closure refuses a chain (consumer of a consumer)

K2_value.rule: the shared value is the producer's retained rows: K after k_norm and RoPE, V after the parameter-free v_norm (or K-derived per the producer's v_from_k), one row per absolute position, written once, by the producer

K3_positions.rule: rows are indexed by the absolute position of the component's token stream. RoPE is applied once, at the producer, with the producer's PositionPolicy. The consumer rotates only Q, with its own policy, at the query's absolute position. Admission requires PositionPolicy equality (kind, theta, rotary_fraction, basis), else KvSourcePositionMismatch
tests: positions after a chunk boundary carry absolute indices (C-CHUNK)

K4_geometry.rule: equal head_dim and num_kv_heads, and consumer num_q_heads divisible by num_kv_heads, else KvSourceGeometryMismatch

K5_consumer_policy.rule: the consumer applies its OWN mask kind, window, causality, score scale and softcap over the producer's rows; nothing about the producer's mask is inherited
tests: a fixture whose consumer has a distinct score scale changes output (causal operand)

K6_retention.rule: producer retention = the union of HistoryRange over the producer and all its consumers; a provider evicts a row only when no member of the union requires it
tests: retention computed for a fixture with consumers that need more than the producer would need alone is the union (unit, on the planner); evicted rows are never read (WindowKvState fixture with window crossing)

K7_span_interactions.sliding_consumer_of_full_producer: REFUSED in this rung: KvSourceSpanMismatch. Well-defined (the producer already retains everything and the consumer applies its own window), but no checkpoint needs it in a geometry- and position-compatible form, because Gemma's sliding and full layers differ in head_dim and RoPE, and admitting it would add an unexercised mask/retention path
K7_span_interactions.full_consumer_of_sliding_producer: REFUSED in this rung: KvSourceSpanMismatch. Under K6 it would force the producer's provider to retain beyond the producer's own window, which changes the producer's memory class; refused until a model needs it
tests: one refusal fixture per refused case, refusal by name
K7_span_interactions.widening: only by a new dated section with its own fixture and oracle

K8_ordering.rule: within a step the producer runs before the consumer; in batch prefill the producer appends the whole chunk before any consumer reads

K9_step_contract.rule: AttentionStepCall::reading(producer_view, position) requires producer_view.end() == position + 1, splits the last row off as the fresh K/V, and hands the kernel the same shape an own-KV step gets; AttentionStepCall::new is unchanged
tests: refusal when the producer has not appended position p
refusal when the producer view is short of the consumer's required start

K10_providers.rule: consumers are LayerContinuationGeometry::Stateless; a provider declares whether it serves shared history; canonical and window providers do; codec providers refuse a program with consumers by name (CodecProviderSharedHistoryUnsupported) until a CODEC rung measures it
tests: canonical and window providers pass V4

K11_rollback_verify.rule: truncation acts on producers only; after rollback to p a consumer reads exactly producer rows < p; verify-N acceptance and rejection behave as for own-KV layers
tests: rollback mid-decode then re-decode equals a fresh run (V4 tolerances)
verify-N with a rejected suffix leaves producer length = accepted length

K12_memory.rule: KV bytes = the sum over producers of retained rows x row bytes; consumers contribute 0

K13_device.rule: consumers allocate no K/V buffers and bind the producer's buffers
tests: same-allocation identity check on lowered Metal

K14_distributed.rule: a layer-sharded plan that places a consumer and its producer on different shards is refused by name in this rung

layer_input_stream_contract.P1_declaration: Component.layer_input_stream {slice_width, layers, sources[TokenLookup{object, scale}, EmbeddingProjection{object, prenorm_scale, norm (per slice, weighted, eps)}], combine_scale, injection{site: AfterFfnResidual, form: GatedProjection{activation, post_norm}}}. Every scale is a declared value, never folded into weights: sqrt(256)=16 lookup scale (exact), hidden_size^-0.5 pre-norm scale, 2^-0.5 combine, per the HF oracle
layer_input_stream_contract.P2_token_ids: the stream is computed in the prelude from the TEXT token id of each position. A position with no text token id (an embedding-only entry, an image or audio soft token) is REFUSED by name (LayerInputStreamNeedsTokenId) in this rung; nothing is zero-filled or reverse-mapped
layer_input_stream_contract.P3_injection: after the FFN residual add and before layer_scale; slice i to layer i; gate -> gelu_tanh -> multiply by slice -> project -> weighted RMSNorm -> residual add
layer_input_stream_contract.P4_residency: the token lookup table is a lookup-only residency class: host-mapped, read one row per position, never device-resident, never counted in device weight budgets

preservation.P-PRES1: every tensor in the container carries provenance {source repo, revision, tensor name, source dtype, source shape, sha256 of the source bytes} and a class in {active, retained_unreachable}; canonical encodings of either class are byte-exact preserved originals
preservation.P-PRES2: byte-exact recovery: each retained tensor read back from the container has the source sha256 (test at R6, when weights are first read)
preservation.P-PRES3: unreachability: the op plan may reference only active tensors. (a) retained roles appear in no operand table; (b) closure at encode AND at open refuses any OperandRef to a retained tensor with ClosureDefect::RetainedTensorBound; (c) negative test: mutating a consumer to KvSource::Own must be refused with RetainedTensorBound, never bind k_proj; (d) negative test: a forged op plan binding a retained tensor is refused at open
preservation.P-PRES4: every retained tensor carries a reason the graph still justifies (ShadowedByKvSource{layer} requires that layer's kv_source to be Layer), else ClosureDefect::RetainedWithoutReason
preservation.P-PRES5: retained tensors are never prepared or loaded for execution and are excluded from execution residency budgets; they are counted separately in the operand census

kv_cache_bytes_bf16.rule: computed from the header geometry: per producer, rows = min(ctx, 512) for sliding and ctx for full, x 2 (K,V) x num_kv_heads x head_dim x 2 bytes. V6 asserts exact equality with provider-reported bytes at a BF16 provider; an f32 provider reports exactly 2x

retained_unreachable_bytes.rule: bf16 bytes of k_proj + v_proj + k_norm on every KvSource::Layer layer, from the headers

how_this_can_be_wrong_in_a_way_the_tests: HF and Google agree on producers only by coincidence of layout; a future checkpoint where they disagree is refused, which is correct but means the graph's producers rest on the HF rule

every V1 pass relies on NC-KV and NC-PLE failing; if the oracle's wrong arms are themselves near-identical on the bank (e.g. sharing barely matters on short prompts), the controls must fail on the long sequences or the bank is too weak
the near-tie margin tau = 2x the logprob tolerance; a systematic offset below tolerance could still reorder near-ties consistently, which tie_swap records but does not fail
